name: Rollin L. Ford
current_role: Independent Director, Symbotic Inc. (since ~2022); retired Walmart EVP & Chief Administrative Officer
profile: Rollin Ford spent 33 years at Walmart, where he held several executive roles including Chief Logistics Officer, CIO (2006-2012) and finally EVP & Chief Administrative Officer, before retiring in 2016. He now sits on the board of warehouse-robotics firm Symbotic, in which Walmart is a major customer and shareholder.
interesting_fact: He ran IT for the world's largest retailer as Walmart's CIO from 2006 to 2012, after years running its logistics network as Chief Logistics Officer.
deep_cut_fact: He began at Walmart as an intern in 1983 and moved onto a distribution-center floor role in 1984 before rising to the C-suite; he holds a B.S. from Taylor University.
notes: Low public profile; board member, not executive. The Walmart careers article on his intern-to-exec path (deep-cut source) now returns 404 - verify via archive before quoting. Also reportedly on boards of Mercy Health and John Brown University (CB Insights). Strong fit for supply-chain automation angle.

name: Terrance Lane Wilson
current_role: Senior Vice President & General Counsel, The Williams Companies (since April 2017)
profile: T. Lane Wilson is Williams' top lawyer, overseeing legal, government affairs, outreach and compliance at the Tulsa-based natural-gas pipeline giant. Before joining in 2017 he was a U.S. Magistrate Judge for the Northern District of Oklahoma, and earlier a partner at Tulsa firm Hall Estill; his wealth reflects Williams stock awards.
interesting_fact: He went from the federal bench straight to the C-suite: a sitting U.S. Magistrate Judge whom Chief Justice John Roberts had appointed to the Judicial Conference Committee on Criminal Law in 2016, he left to become Williams' general counsel in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Before law, he was an engineer: he earned an electrical-engineering degree from the University of Tulsa (1989), where he played varsity tennis and won an individual conference championship, then worked for Exxon before law school.
notes: Goes by 'T. Lane Wilson'. In-house lawyer rather than entrepreneur; relevant for gas/power-for-data-centers angle (Williams has power JV work for data centers). Route via Williams media relations.

name: Vito S Pantilione
current_role: President, CEO & Director, Parke Bancorp / Parke Bank (Sewell, NJ)
profile: Vito Pantilione co-founded Parke Bank, which opened in January 1999, and has run it as President & CEO ever since (and its holding company Parke Bancorp since 2005). He grew the South Jersey community bank to over $2 billion in assets; earlier he owned mortgage firms Eagle Valley and Interstate Mortgage Management and was President of First Commercial Bank of Philadelphia (1991-94).
interesting_fact: Parke Bank turned a profit in only its 13th month of operation and, per the bank, has been profitable every quarter since; it has repeatedly ranked among the top-performing community banks in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: He received an honorary doctorate from Philadelphia University for his work in finance and banking, and served on the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's Community Depository Institution Advisory Council.

name: Jugal K. Vijayvargiya
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Materion Corporation (since March 2017); Independent Director, Sensata Technologies
profile: Jugal Vijayvargiya has run Cleveland-area advanced-materials maker Materion since 2017. Before that he spent 26 years at Delphi Automotive, rising through engineering, sales and general management in Europe and North America to lead its $3B Electronics & Safety segment from Germany as an officer and Executive Committee member.
interesting_fact: Materion, which he leads, supplies niche materials central to energy and computing: beryllium products, semiconductor sputtering targets and thin-film materials, and even materials for molten-salt nuclear reactors.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineer by training, he holds both his bachelor's and master's in electrical engineering from The Ohio State University, and ran Delphi's $3B electronics business from a base in Germany before becoming a CEO.
notes: Good fit for semiconductor/data-center supply-chain and advanced-nuclear materials angle. Also a director of the Greater Cleveland Partnership. Degree fields per search summaries of Materion bio; Conference Board bio confirms Delphi details.

name: Stephen Yalof
current_role: President, CEO & Director, Tanger Inc. (NYSE: SKT)
profile: Stephen Yalof has led outlet and open-air shopping-center REIT Tanger since January 2021, after joining as President & COO in April 2020 and succeeding Steven Tanger. A 25+ year retail-real-estate veteran, he previously was CEO of Simon Premium Outlets and held real-estate leadership roles at Ralph Lauren and The Gap; Tanger now operates centers in 22 U.S. states and Canada.

He sits on the advisory board of George Washington University's Center for Real Estate Studies, at his alma mater (B.S. Business Administration).
notes: Media-friendly CEO who regularly does national TV - likely receptive to podcast invites via ICR. 'First non-family CEO' is inferred from Tanger succession history (founder Stanley Tanger, then son Steven); verify before quoting.

current_role: Chief Executive Officer, The Boots Group (since Sycamore Partners' 2025 take-private of Walgreens Boots Alliance)
profile: Italian-born, Monaco-based pharmacist Ornella Barra built regional drug distributor Di Pharma, sold it to Stefano Pessina's Alleanza Salute, and rose with him through Alliance Santé, Alliance UniChem, Alliance Boots and Walgreens Boots Alliance, where she was COO International. name: John Hanke
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Niantic Spatial (stepped back from CEO in March 2026)
profile: Texan entrepreneur John Hanke co-founded Keyhole (sold to Google in 2004, becoming Google Earth), led Google's Geo division (Maps, Street View), then built Niantic Labs inside Google and spun it out in 2015, launching Ingress and Pokemon Go. After Niantic's games business was sold to Scopely in 2025, he took its geospatial platform into Niantic Spatial, a geospatial-AI startup.
interesting_fact: Keyhole, his 2001 mapping startup, was backed by the CIA's venture arm In-Q-Tel, Sony and NVIDIA before Google bought it and turned it into Google Earth; Pokemon Go has since generated over $8.8B in player spending.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he spent four years in the U.S. Foreign Service, including a posting in Myanmar; then, while at Berkeley Haas, he joined Archetype Interactive, maker of Meridian 59 - one of the first commercial MMORPGs - which sold to 3DO on the day he got his MBA. He grew up in tiny Cross Plains, Texas.
notes: Strong podcast fit (geospatial AI, large world models, AR). Hurun lists Niantic at $4B but games unit was sold to Scopely in 2025. Myanmar/Meridian 59 details from Wikipedia citing CNBC/Forbes; 3DO sale-on-graduation-day anecdote per Wikipedia (Engel 2014, Forbes 2016).

name: Daniel Krauss
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Information Officer & Chief HR Officer, Flix SE (FlixBus/FlixTrain/Greyhound), Munich
profile: Daniel Krauss co-founded FlixBus in Munich in 2011 with Jochen Engert and Andre Schwammlein, betting on Germany's planned deregulation of long-distance buses. As CIO and CHRO he oversees Flix's technology and people as it grew into an international mobility group spanning FlixBus, FlixTrain, Greyhound and Kamil Koc. He also invests in and advises startups.
interesting_fact: The three co-founders met at university and began sketching the FlixBus idea in 2009, when Germany announced plans to deregulate intercity buses; Flix later bought America's Greyhound Lines (2021) and says it has carried 500+ million passengers.
deep_cut_fact: He is a committed backer of entrepreneurship education: an active shareholder in STARTUP TEENS, Germany's largest NGO for entrepreneurial education, a co-shareholder and trustee of Berlin's CODE University, and a frequent lecturer at Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen.
notes: Not to be confused with German actor Daniel Krauss (de.wikipedia). Flix is tech-heavy (in-house routing/pricing platform) - good entrepreneurship/mobility angle; Flix has also piloted e-buses.
